im-fadenkreuz-europa.selector: #part_test: Ziel des Spiels / Spielaufbau / Spielablauf only

components.role: Unchanged independent 2 September 2008 Reich der Spiele review by Armando Schmidt, matching Noris/Steinwender/Puhl, 110 double-sided cards, three ring sizes and coordinate strings. Corroborating identity/mechanism evidence, not publisher instructions or a complete question deck.

im-fadenkreuz-europa.evidence: Detailed German Cliquenabend rules account for Noris’s 2008 Europa-Wissen by Arno Steinwender and Christoph Puhl, successfully retrieved unchanged from its actual public game page. This is the named Im Fadenkreuz: Europa, BGG 37730: cached primary BGG metadata explicitly lists Europa-Wissen as its alternate name, and authors/year/publisher plus rings/map/coordinate-string mechanism match. No ID change or substitution of 2009 Deutschland-Wissen, the unrelated Kosmos Europa quiz, or political/military games. The complete selected Ziel des Spiels, Spielaufbau and Spielablauf sections were read, ending before the separate Strategie/opinion section. An independently retrieved Reich der Spiele review dated 2 September 2008 corroborates the same game, authors, 110 double-sided question cards and coordinate-string/ring solution mechanism. Account supplies string threading, central map, three differently sized coloured rings and score marker per player, 110 cards/220 questions, starter’s die and rotation, die-selected ordinary/speed/double-points rounds, choosing/reading/showing the picture question, sequential normal ring placement with overlap allowed, coordinate-string answer reveal, 2/3/5 points for large/medium/small rings containing the correct intersection, zero for misses, country-question small-ring/two-point plus opponent-miss bonuses, no repositioning, simultaneous speed placement with extra points for correct rings covered by later rings, double scoring and score-threshold ending. Accurate source is a THIRD-PARTY RULES REFERENCE HTML in original German, not an English translation or recovered publisher manual. The reviewer’s parenthesized suggestion to always use the top question is explicitly commentary, retained and not silently promoted to an official rule. Important original inconsistency: the goal section says 30 points or more ends play; the final sentence says more than30 points. Both are preserved verbatim, and the exact threshold boundary is not resolved or invented. Full first-player selection, simultaneous threshold/tie handling, every country/die interaction and all publisher edge cases are not independently established. The actual coordinate map, question/answer cards, die and rings remain necessary; the complete question deck is not reproduced. The official current Noris manual archive was separately checked through all three advertised pages and its exact-product public search. No matching Europa/606104536 manual link appears; a bounded historical index for that rules subdomain also yielded no matching record. This is limited discovery, not proof no original manual exists. Canonical selected HTML text normalizes whitespace only and excludes navigation, later strategy/reviews and unrelated games; unchanged main/supporting HTML retain hashes. Linked WMV was not needed or executed. One specific MAJOR deck-exhaustion ending finding is recorded; the source’s own threshold ambiguity remains explicit. No full publisher-rulebook audit, PASS or summary-body repair.
